name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Fedorchak is an incumbent with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Fedorchak's incumbency, and her roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage over Trygve Hammer all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets agree at about 96% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings signaling otherwise, there is no basis to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or a scandal involving Fedorchak could tighten the race, though nothing currently suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+18. First-term incumbent Julie Fedorchak is running for reelection and has been renominated by her party. She has raised about $1.7 million and holds over $1 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Trygve Hammer has raised roughly $190,000 with under $100,000 on hand. Two independent candidates also appear on the ballot but show no fundraising activity.

No public general-election polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 96% chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong lean, incumbency, and financial dominance makes this a Safe Republican seat, with the only real question being the size of the margin.
